title: Invariant during the backward sweep
statement: Let $W$ and $M$ be finite binary Turing machines, let $a$ be a natural number, and let $x$ be a finite word over the schedule alphabet. Let $c$ be a configuration of the schedule machine, $u\in\mathbb{Z}$, $R,n\in\mathbb{N}$ with $n\le 2R+1$, an optional state $q$ of $M$, a bit $b$, payload vectors $\mathrm{read}$ and $f(z)$ for each $z\in\mathbb{Z}$, tape contents $T$, and output word $o$. Assume the guide tape of $c$ is the fixed guide of radius $R$, every decoded current payload of $T$ at coordinate $z$ and lane $i$ equals $f(z)_i$, and for $-R\le z\le R$ every decoded cached left-neighbor payload equals $f(z-1)_i$. Then there exist tape contents $T'$ such that after $n$ steps from the backward-phase configuration at guide position $R$, with neighbor registers $f(R+1)$, the configuration is in the backward phase at position $R-n$, with registers $f(R-n+1)$ and the same base configuration and output. For every lane $i$ and coordinate $z$, the decoded current payload in $T'$ is $f(z+m_i)_i$ when $R-n<z\le R$, and is $f(z)_i$ otherwise, where $m_i$ is the virtual-head movement selected from $q$ and $\mathrm{read}$. Moreover, for $-R\le z\le R-n$, the decoded cached left-neighbor payload in $T'$ is $f(z-1)_i$.
hypotheses_covered: Guide tape of $c$ equals the radius-$R$ guide
Decoded current payloads of $T$ equal $f(z)$ at every coordinate and lane
Decoded cached left-neighbor payloads equal $f(z-1)$ for coordinates in $[-R,R]$
